name: How do counter-depth and standard-depth refrigerators compare in layout planning?

mainEntity.name: How do counter-depth and standard-depth refrigerators compare in layout planning?

acceptedAnswer.text: Standard counter-depth refrigerators sit almost flush with 24-inch deep base cabinets, creating clean sightlines and preventing traffic blockages in narrow walkways. However, they cost more per cubic foot and offer less internal storage capacity compared to freestanding units. Standard-depth models provide maximum interior food storage at a lower price point, but their cases extend roughly four to six inches past surrounding countertops. If your layout features an island opposite the fridge, you must confirm there is adequate clearance for doors to swing open without blocking movement through the room.
acceptedAnswer.description: Counter-depth fridges sit flush with cabinets for sleeker walkways but offer less storage capacity. Standard-depth models provide more cubic footage but protrude past adjacent countertops.
